textual_enrichment.core_textual_profile: G1 expresses qualified acceptance of everyday food choices: familiar taste, manageable price and practical convenience are appreciated, while restricted choice and uncertainty about ingredients or environmental impact limit an unreserved endorsement.
dominant_themes: doubts about ingredient quality and range of choice
textual_enrichment.internal_diversity: The comments emphasize different practical benefits and reservations rather than a single priority; some qualify their generally balanced assessment as not applying to every purchase. The corpus contains only four distinct formulations despite 32 observations, limiting the depth of independent discourse variation that can be inferred.

textual_enrichment.core_textual_profile: G2 describes a purchasing experience valued for choice, perceived quality and time saving, but assessed conditionally against excess spending, continued price comparison and unreliable delivery.
dominant_themes: online time saving constrained by delivery reliability
textual_enrichment.internal_diversity: Some comments focus on variety and quality despite spending more than planned, others remain price-conscious despite satisfaction, and online convenience is qualified by unreliable delivery; several statements explicitly indicate that their assessment does not apply to every purchase. The 32 observations contain only six distinct formulations.

textual_enrichment.core_textual_profile: G3 conveys conditional appreciation of food offers: positive experiences and perceived quality coexist with doubts about whether price is justified, whether environmental claims can be verified and whether local alternatives are accessible.
dominant_themes: appreciation of quality with uncertain environmental claims
textual_enrichment.internal_diversity: The main reservations concern different constraints—price, verifiability of environmental claims and access to local products—rather than a uniform rejection of the offer. Some respondents explicitly qualify their judgments as varying across purchases. The 32 comments contain only five distinct formulations, limiting claims about the diversity of independent viewpoints.
